subject: Proposal: 2-year strategic prepay with phased consumption floors
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@optiscale.com>
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 25 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: 2-year prepay idea + ramp floors (pricing ask)

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week — OptiScale is excited about Redwood's latency profile and the prefix caching features. We're putting together a procurement proposal for a 2-year commitment and wanted to surface the deal structure we're considering and ask for a run-rate discount that makes multi-year prepay compelling for our CFO.

High-level ask:
- Commitment: $1.2M total prepay over 24 months (equivalent to ~$50k/month average).
- Preferred billing: annual prepay (one invoice per year), but open to split-invoice if needed.
- Ramp profile: first 6 months at 60% of the committed run-rate, months 7–12 at 85%, remainder at 100% (we expect usage to materialize after Q2).
- Request: 22% term discount off list on the 2-year prepay vs standard monthly pricing, with the option to allocate spend across models.

We also have a few procurement constraints: our CFO wants consumption floors tied to quarterly checkpoints (i.e., minimum consumption to avoid clawbacks) and prefers quarterly reconciliations rather than monthly. Can you share an initial term sheet and whether the 22% is within range?

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Emma
Emma Jones
Head of Cloud & Platform
OptiScale

Attachments: OptiScale-Consumption-Forecast.xlsx (forecast by quarter)
From: evelyn.hart@redwood.com
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@optiscale.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 25 Jan 2027 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: 2-year prepay idea + ramp floors (pricing ask)

Hi Emma — great to hear from you and thanks for the clear ask.

We can definitely structure a 2-year prepay with phased floors. High-level response:
- A 22% off list is towards the high end for a $1.2M two-year prepay (effectively $600k/year), but it's not out of the question if we set reasonable protections (consumption floors, quarterly reconciliations, and a clause for reversion to standard rates if run-rate is significantly below forecast after the ramp).
- We'd prefer annual invoicing for simplicity; split invoicing is also doable but may change the discount profile.
- Typical approach that has worked: 15–18% baseline for this size + an incremental performance credit tied to meeting ramp checkpoints (i.e., additional 3–7% if you meet 85%+ by month 12). That lets us protect the unit economics while giving you upside for delivering consumption.

I'll pull in finance and pricing to get an explicit proposal. Can you confirm whether OptiScale requires a true irrevocable prepay (funds paid up front) or whether a committed annual purchase order with annual invoicing is acceptable? That affects treasury and discount calculus.

I'll follow up once I have an initial term sheet.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Sr. Director, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attachment: -- none --
From: Oliver Green <oliver.green@optiscale.com>
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.com, Emma Jones <emma.jones@optiscale.com>
Date: Tue, 26 Jan 2027 08:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: 2-year prepay idea + ramp floors (pricing ask)

Evelyn / Emma — quick note from engineering side. The ramp profile Emma sent is conservative; we expect production rollout to accelerate after our feature flag opens in May, which is why we proposed the stepped ramp. A couple clarifications for your pricing team:
- We need the prepay to be usable across both chat and embedding models, and ideally transferable between model families during the contract.
- For the quarterly reconciliation, OptiScale's procurement team insists on a minimum quarterly floor (to avoid clawbacks mid-contract). That floor can step up across years (i.e., 45%/60%/75% of annualized quarter in Y1 -> Y2), but it can't be zero.

If it helps, we can provide a short letter from finance confirming the forecast.

Thanks,
Oliver
CTO, OptiScale
From: evelyn.hart@redwood.com
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 27 Jan 2027 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: 2-year prepay idea + ramp floors (pricing ask) — request for discount approval

Team — forwarding OptiScale's ask. TL;DR: $1.2M over 24 months; customer asks for ~22% term discount; proposes phased quarterly floors and annual invoicing. They need model portability across chat/embedding. Forecast attached.

My suggested approach (to approve internally):
- Offer structure: 16% baseline term discount for 2-year annual prepay (irrevocable up-front or PO-led annual invoice).
- Ramp performance credit: additional 4–6% applied as a rebate at year-end if OptiScale hits the agreed ramp checkpoints (85% by month 12, 95% by month 18).
- Consumption floors: set quarterly minimums tied to a % of annualized quarter; clawback applied only at annual reconciliation (not monthly) to meet procurement ask.
- Model portability: allow allocation across Redwood model families with a list of covered SKUs; overage rates priced at standard monthly list.

Approval ask: sign off on 20% max effective discount (baseline + performance credits), with final legal term sheet to include the quarterly floor language and PO/invoicing options. If approved, I'll prepare the term sheet and DocuSign.

Note: treasury would prefer annual PO/invoice vs irreversible prepay; if we can accept a PO structure we should price slightly tighter.

Thanks — Evelyn

Attachment: Redwood_TermSheet_OptiScale_v1.pdf (draft term sheet, redline-ready)
From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 3 Feb 2027 15:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: 2-year prepay idea + ramp floors (pricing ask) — request for discount approval

Thanks for the clear recommendation, Evelyn. I approve moving forward with the proposed structure with the following conditions:

1) Cap the upfront contractual discount exposure at 20% effective (baseline + max performance payout).
2) Annual invoicing with an option for irrevocable prepay if customer requests, but baseline quote should assume PO-based annual invoicing (this protects our cash assumptions).
3) Quarterly floors acceptable, but any clawback must be annualized and can be remedied by a one-time true-up at contract year-end. No monthly clawbacks.
4) Model portability OK limited to Redwood-curated model list (to be enumerated in the term sheet).
5) Include a 60-day ramp review clause that allows us to convert to monthly overage pricing if actual usage is <40% of forecast at the 6-month checkpoint.

Evelyn — proceed to finalize term sheet and send to OptiScale. Ben/Laura — loop in Legal and Finance for final language; aim to get DocuSign-ready draft this week.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Commercial & Strategy
Redwood Inference
